title: Etale structure-sheaf cohomology in smooth proper curve families
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme (quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]) [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to S$ a proper smooth morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with nonempty geometrically connected fibres [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] of dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}}$ and $\mathcal O_{S,\mathrm{et}}$ be the associated etale structure-module sheaves [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module], placed in the same coefficient universe as the abelian direct-image and Artin--Schreier functors. If a universe lift is used, each section group is $\operatorname{ULift}(\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V))$ with the transported addition and scalar action; the same sectionwise lift is used for $E_{\mathrm{et}}$ below. The natural map $\mathcal O_{S,\mathrm{et}}\to f_*\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}}$ is an isomorphism. There is a finite locally free $\mathcal O_S$-module $E$ (Zariski-locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_S^{\oplus r}$ for a finite integer $r$ allowed to vary between opens) with
$$R^1f_*\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}}\cong E_{\mathrm{et}}$$
as $\mathcal O_{S,\mathrm{et}}$-modules. These higher direct images are computed in abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], with the natural scalar action induced by multiplication by pullbacks of base functions; $E_{\mathrm{et}}$ is as in [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module].

source.place: Tag 0GKA, label lemma-genus-in-nodal-family-of-curves, (a),(b), smooth-curve specialization; etale form using Tag 03P2, etale-cohomology.tex, label theorem-zariski-fpqc-quasi-coherent; the same assertion with a sectionwise coefficient-universe lift

proof.text: Smoothness gives flatness and local finite presentation. Properness gives quasi-compactness and separatedness, hence quasi-separatedness, so $f$ is of finite presentation. Smooth fibres are geometrically reduced. For every $s\in S$ the fibre $X_s$ is proper by proper base-change permanence, geometrically reduced and geometrically connected. Apply the field global-sections lemma to its structure morphism to get the canonical isomorphism $\kappa(s)\to H^0(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$. These conclusions require no reducedness of $S$. The quasi-separatedness just used is elementary from the definitions: a closed immersion is affine by the conventions node, so its inverse image of any affine open is affine and therefore quasi-compact; apply this to the diagonal of $f$.

source.place: Tag 0GKA, proof of (a); Tag 0E0L and Tag 0E62 hypotheses

proof.text: Put $K=Rf_*\mathcal O_X[0]$ in the Zariski module derived category. The structure module is finitely presented as a module (locally it is free of rank one), and flat over $S$ by Step 1. Thus the perfect-direct-image theorem makes $K$ perfect and identifies $Lg^*K$ with $Rf_{T,*}\mathcal O_{X_T}[0]$ for every base change $g:T\to S$. The flat derived structure-unit lemma supplies $u:\mathcal O_S[0]\to K$ inducing $f^\sharp$ on $H^0$, with no negative derived fibre cohomology and with $H^0(Li_s^*u)$ invertible by Step 1. Apply the perfect degree-zero fibre criterion. It proves that the natural $f^\sharp:\mathcal O_S\to f_*\mathcal O_X$ is an isomorphism and, locally on $S$, $K\cong\mathcal O_S[0]\oplus P$ with $P$ perfect of Tor amplitude in $[1,\infty)$.

source.place: Tag 0GKA, first two sentences of proof; Tags 0B91 and 0E62

proof.text: Fix one open carrying this decomposition and $s$ in it. Derived base change gives $H^i(Li_s^*K)=H^i(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$; for $i\ge1$ this is $H^i(Li_s^*P)$, and the latter vanishes for $i\le0$ by its Tor amplitude. The fibre is Noetherian of dimension one: it is finite type and quasi-compact over the field $\kappa(s)$ by properness, and is locally Noetherian by the locally-finite-type lemma (a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field). The dimension-one hypothesis is exactly the given fibre dimension. The Noetherian dimension-vanishing theorem gives $H^i(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})=0$ for $i>1$. The perfect finite-free residue-model lemma applied to $P$ therefore gives, on an affine neighbourhood of $s$, a representative having only one nonzero term, a finite free module in degree one. Its cohomology in degree one is that module and all its other cohomology is zero. Define globally $E=H^1(K)=R^1f_*\mathcal O_X$ in Zariski modules; the local models show $E$ is finite locally free, with rank possibly varying, and $K$ locally is $\mathcal O_S[0]\oplus E[-1]$. Here $E[-1]$ means $E$ placed in cohomological degree one.

source.place: Tag 0GKA, fibre vanishing and final perfect-complex argument; Tags 02UZ and 0BCD

proof.text: For any $g:T\to S$, pull back the local models from Step 3. Both $\mathcal O_S$ and $E$ are locally free, so ordinary tensor pullback computes their derived pullback: tensoring a free module is a finite direct sum of the identity functor and has no higher Tor. The canonical derived base-change isomorphism of Step 2 consequently induces the canonical isomorphisms $f_{T,*}\mathcal O_{X_T}\cong\mathcal O_T$ and $R^1f_{T,*}\mathcal O_{X_T}\cong g^*E$, and the higher Zariski direct images vanish. In particular take an affine etale $v:V\to S$. The Leray spectral sequence for $f_V:X_V\to V$, together with affine vanishing for the quasi-coherent modules $\mathcal O_V$ and $v^*E$, gives the canonical edge isomorphism $H^1(X_V,\mathcal O_{X_V})\cong\Gamma(V,v^*E)$. All maps here are the canonical base-change and edge maps, so their compositions with the usual cohomology pullback for $W\to V$ are the section pullbacks for $E$; the base-change map is obtained from the adjunction unit and its composition law. In degree zero the same construction is exactly structural pullback $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)\to\Gamma(X_V,\mathcal O_{X_V})$, and is bijective. Explicitly, write $j_V:X_V\to X$ and $j_W:X_W\to X_V$ for a tower over $W\xrightarrow{h}V\xrightarrow{v}S$. The transpose defining the direct-image comparison for the composite is $Rf_*\eta_{j_Vj_W}$. Under the composition isomorphisms the composite adjunction unit is $\eta_{j_V}$ followed by $Rj_{V,*}(\eta_{j_W})$ after pullback. Thus transposing the two successive base-change maps gives the same map as transposing the composite; taking $H^1$ and sections gives the displayed restriction compatibility. For structure modules, the additional derived-to-ordinary comparison is transposed from the ordinary unit, whose section formula is successive structural pullback, so the same unit identity applies. The affine Leray edge identification is evaluation of this derived direct-image identification; its functoriality is consequently this equality, rather than a choice of fibrewise isomorphisms. The choice-independence and composition clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-functorial] identify these section maps with the cohomology maps of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]. Indeed, in its resolution notation the map is H^1(Gamma(beta)) followed by the inverse of H^1(Gamma(lambda)); this is precisely the global-sections image of the same derived adjunction-unit arrow, as in Remark 01FB. Thus the equality of unit arrows just proved is an equality for the specified cohomology pullbacks, independently of the resolutions used.

source.place: Tag 0GKA, base-change compatibility; Tag 0B91; Tags 01F2 and 01XB; Section 01F7, Lemma 01F8 (lemma-functoriality) and Remark 01FB (remark-explain-arrow), for the normalized resolution cohomology maps

proof.text: Let $A$ be the associated additive structure sheaf in the fixed coefficient universe of the abelian direct-image functor, and $\mathcal P(V)=H^1(X_V{}_{\mathrm{et}},A|_{X_V})$. The higher-direct-image presheaf theorem identifies $R^1f_*A$ with $\mathcal P^\#$. For affine etale $V$, $X_V$ is quasi-compact separated: $f_V$ is proper by proper permanence and $V$ is affine. Its restricted coefficient sheaf is the same associated structure sheaf, with the same sectionwise lift, since both assign the (possibly lifted) ring of functions to every etale object. Apply the pullback-natural comparison to $X_V,\mathcal O_{X_V}$, then Step 4, then the sectionwise lift if used. This gives bijections $b_V:\mathcal P(V)\to L\Gamma(V,v^*E)$. For every arrow between affine etale base objects, the new comparison's pullback square and the canonical coherent edge/base-change maps from Step 4 give $b_W\operatorname{res}_{W,V}=\rho_{W,V}b_V$. For a base function $a$, apply the comparison's coefficient naturality to multiplication by $f_V^*a$; the coherent edge and base-change maps are linear: they are induced by morphisms of complexes of modules over $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, so on cycles they send $a z$ to $a$ times the image of $z$, and this equality passes to the quotient by boundaries. Thus $b_V(a x)=a b_V(x)$, with transported scalar action if lifted. No cohomology in one universe is identified with another without this explicit comparison.

source.place: Tag 03P2, separated-case comparison; Tag 03Q8 higher-direct-image presheaf

proof.text: Extend the compatible $b_V$ to a presheaf morphism $b:\mathcal P\to E_{\mathrm{et}}$ as follows. For an arbitrary etale object $U$, restrict a cohomology class to an affine open cover of $U$, apply $b_V$ on each member, and glue in $E_{\mathrm{et}}$. The target is a sheaf by quasi-coherent descent. Compatibility is checked after covering every overlap by affine opens, so the glued section is independent of the cover and is compatible with every etale arrow; for an arrow, cover its source by affine opens lying over affine opens of its target. The affine-opens-basis lemma provides all these covers, which are etale coverings by the definition of the small site. The same argument proves linearity of $b$. On every affine object $b$ is bijective by Step 5. Hence $b$ is locally injective and locally surjective: restrict any equality or desired target section to an affine open cover and use those bijections. The locally-bijective sheafification criterion now gives $\mathcal P^\#\cong E_{\mathrm{et}}$ as abelian sheaves. The map and its inverse are module-linear (apply the bijection to $a x$ to check the inverse), so it is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{S,\mathrm{et}}$-modules. For degree zero, take the natural structural map $\mathcal O_{S,\mathrm{et}}\to f_*\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}}$. Both sides are sheaves, and its components on affine etale objects are bijective by Step 4 and the degree-zero comparison in Step 5. To prove injectivity on any object, restrict two sections with equal images to an affine open cover and use those bijections, then the sheaf uniqueness axiom. To prove surjectivity, lift a target section on that cover using the bijections; on overlaps the lifts agree after an affine refinement by injectivity, hence agree as sheaf sections and glue to a preimage. Thus this natural map is an isomorphism. This proves both conclusions, including an empty base and rank-zero local models.
